claims.text: A recording rule lets Prometheus evaluate a PromQL expression and save its result as a new set of time series, with the metric name given by `record`; the expression is evaluated at each evaluation cycle.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Configuration > Recording rules (Recording rules; <rule> record/expr)

claims.text: Prometheus reads rules from the files listed under `rule_files` in its configuration; the entries are globs, and rules are read from all matching files.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Configuration > Configuration file (rule_files); Recording rules (Configuring rules)

claims.text: Rules exist in rule groups; the rules within a group run sequentially at a regular interval, with the same evaluation time.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Configuration > Recording rules (Recording rules: 'Rules within a group are run sequentially...')

claims.text: The recorded series keeps the labels of the expression's result (plus any `labels` the rule adds); `sum by (job)` leaves only the `job` label, so each recorded share carries only `job`.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Recording rules (<rule> labels); Querying > Operators (Aggregation operators, by)

claims.text: Rules are evaluated on schedule whether or not anyone queries the result; each evaluation adds one sample to the recorded series (every 15 s on staging).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Recording rules (evaluated at regular interval); prometheus.yaml line 53 at stage-4

claims.text: Recording rules are computed by Prometheus from samples it already stores; the scraped target's /metrics output does not change.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Recording rules (precompute expressions, save as new time series)

claims.text: When a new recording rule is created there is no historical data for it; recorded data exists only from when it is evaluated on, unless backfilled with a separate tool (not taught).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Storage > Backfilling for recording rules

claims.text: Staging's Prometheus stores its data in an emptyDir volume, which is deleted when the Pod is replaced. A changed rule file renames the generated ConfigMap and changes the Pod template, so Kubernetes replaces the Pod and the raw data starts again from empty.
claims.source_hint: prometheus.yaml lines 1-5, 130-146 at stage-4; Kubernetes docs: Volumes > emptyDir

claims.text: Staging's Prometheus: scrape_interval 5s, evaluation_interval 15s, rule_files `/etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml` where ConfigMap slo-rules (slo.rules.yml) is mounted.
slo.rules.yml group slo-s3-product-reads records job:product_reads_bad:ratio_rate5m/30m/1h/6h as 1 − (GET product reads without 5xx)/(all GET product reads), sum by (job), the S3 query of slo.md.
claims.source_hint: slo.rules.yml lines 12-21; docs/design/slo.md lines 26, 50-52 at stage-4

claims.text: The scrape job `api` keeps Pods labelled api, api-canary or api-green, so sum by (job) adds the requests of all three Deployments into one share.
claims.source_hint: prometheus.yaml lines 63-78; slo.rules.yml lines 10-11 at stage-4

claims.text: Prometheus documentation recommends recording rule names of the form level:metric:operations: level = aggregation level and labels of the output, operations = operations applied, newest (last applied) first (e.g. ratio_rate5m).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Best practices > Recording rules (Naming and aggregation)

claims.text: Colons in metric names are reserved for user-defined recording rules; exporters and direct instrumentation should not use them.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Concepts > Data model (Metric names and labels, note on colons)

claims.text: slo.rules.yml holds 16 recording rules: order_placement_bad, order_placement_slow, product_reads_bad, refund_requests_slow × 5m/30m/1h/6h, level job; slow ones use a bucket le bound; each group's two alerts pair a short and a long window (5m+1h, 30m+6h).
Writing the bad share once in a recording rule keeps alerts and panels consistent and short when several readers need it continuously; a one-off investigation query is better run directly.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Recording rules (frequently needed expressions); derived from slo.rules.yml header

claims.text: Choices: new SLI S5 → a new group of four rules named in the same form; per-Deployment share → query by app or add rules with app as level, keeping the SLI rules summed by job.
claims.source_hint: derived from slo.rules.yml and prometheus.yaml at stage-4; devops.l4.canary-release

claims.text: On each scrape Prometheus attaches the label job, the configured job name of the target; staging's job is api.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Concepts > Jobs and instances; prometheus.yaml l.63 at stage-4

claims.text: `!~` selects series whose label does not regex-match; regex matches are fully anchored, so api/v1/products.* matches api/v1/products and api/v1/products/{id:int}.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Querying basics (label matchers); docs/design/slo.md l.26 at stage-4
